title: Kenya Inflation Rises to 6.6% as Food and Transport Costs Climb
desc: Kenya's inflation rose to 6.6% in August as higher food, transport and housing costs added pressure to household budgets.
content:
Kenya's annual inflation rose to 6.6% in August 2026, adding fresh pressure to households as the cost of food, transport and other essential services continued to increase.

The latest figures from the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics show that inflation increased from 6.5% recorded in July.

Food and non-alcoholic beverages remained a major source of pressure, recording an annual increase of 9%. Transport costs also rose sharply, increasing by 15.7% over the year.

Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuel-related costs increased by 3.6%, adding to the financial pressure facing households.

The figures help explain why many Kenyans continue to feel the impact of the rising cost of living even when some individual products become cheaper from one month to another.

During August, the prices of some household items declined, including sifted maize flour, tomatoes and diesel. However, increases in other goods and services continued to push overall consumer prices higher.

For households, higher transport costs can quickly affect daily spending, particularly for workers and families that rely on public transport. Rising food prices can also place additional pressure on monthly budgets.

Businesses are also affected when transport and operating costs increase. Companies involved in distribution and logistics may face higher expenses, while smaller businesses can struggle to absorb rising costs without increasing prices.

The August inflation figures also show how changes in fuel and transport costs can spread through the wider economy. When it becomes more expensive to move people and goods, businesses may face additional pressure across their supply chains.

Kenya's inflation remains within the Central Bank's target range, but the latest increase will still be closely watched because of its direct effect on household spending and business costs.

For ordinary consumers, the most important issue remains whether prices of essential goods and services will stabilise in the coming months.

The latest data puts renewed attention on the cost of living and the factors influencing how much Kenyan households spend on food, transport and basic services.
